name: prontera-vendors
author: BlaXun
description: A living player market on Prontera's main road. Fake players run real vending stalls on the inner sidewalks (cards, weapons and armor by class, refined gear, potions, gems, pet eggs, loot from every dungeon and more) and real buying stores on the outer sidewalks that buy your loot: ores, quest turn-ins, junk drops and the loot of every dungeon and leveling field. Prices follow a real server's market (kRO), stalls undercut each other and change as their owners come and go, and everything is tunable in Settings. Needs the population engine switched on.

settings.label: Sell shops
settings.description: Vending stalls selling to you. Off removes them all; the other settings stay as they are.

settings.label: Sell stalls
settings.description: How many sell stalls stand on the inner sidewalks (x=147 and x=164) and the rows east of the fountain (y=110 and y=125). They fill one lane at a time, side by side: north sidewalks first, then south, then the eastern rows. Six staples (potions, general goods, forge supplies, healing items, common and rare cards) are always among them; the rest roll from the other themes. 0 removes them all.

settings.label: Buy shops
settings.description: Buying stores that buy from you: ores, cards, boxes, loot, potions, gems. Off removes them all; the other settings stay as they are.

settings.label: Buy stalls
settings.description: How many buying stores stand on the outer sidewalks (x=140 and x=171) and the rows west of the fountain (y=110 and y=125), one lane at a time, sidewalks first. Eight are always there: two for upgrade ores and one each for crafting materials, elemental stones, herbs, alchemy materials, berries and junk loot. Most others buy a dungeon's or leveling field's loot. 0 removes them all.

settings.label: Minutes before a stall changes
settings.description: How long a vendor stays before packing up; another takes the spot soon after. Each stall varies by up to half this either way so they don't all change at once, and stalls are checked once a minute, at most 8 at a time, so short values run long: 2 means roughly 1 to 5 minutes. A stall that sells out leaves early. 0 keeps them until the server restarts.

settings.label: Price level (%)
settings.description: Every price the stalls ask, as a percentage of the price list (db/population_vendor_prices/prontera-vendors.csv): 100 as listed, 200 twice as much, 50 half. Nothing goes below what an NPC pays for it.

settings.label: Vendors respect the population limit
settings.description: On: stalls count toward the server's fake-player limit and wait for room when it's full. Off: stalls always spawn; they still count, so other fake players fill in a little less while the limit is reached.

settings.label: Vendors shout their wares
settings.description: Stalls call out an item and its price now and then, like "S> Elunium 13K" or "B> Oridecon 9500".

settings.label: Seconds between a stall's shouts
settings.description: On average, per stall; each waits between half and one and a half times this. Stalls also never shout within a few seconds of one another.

settings.label: Customers buy from your stalls
settings.description: Customers visit the vending stalls you open, online or on @autotrade, and buy now and then: steadily at a fair price, fast under market, hardly ever well over it, less when a stall nearby is cheaper. You get the zeny and the usual "sold" message. Off: no extra work for the server.

settings.label: Customers' pace (%)
settings.description: How often customers come to your stalls. At 100 % and a fair price: about one every 20-40 minutes for items fake buyers want (Elunium, Strawberry), every 2 hours for other everyday items, every 3-4 hours for gear and cards; each takes a few. Under market more often, over it far less. 200 = twice as often, 50 = half.

settings.label: Sellers fill your buying stores
settings.description: Players bring loot to the buying stores you open, online or on @autotrade: common drops often, rare ones seldom, more when you offer near the market price, never when an NPC pays as much. Off: no extra work for the server.

settings.label: Sellers' pace (%)
settings.description: How often sellers come to your buying stores. At 100 % and a fair offer: about one every 20 minutes for common loot (Jellopy), every 40-80 minutes for uncommon drops, every 4-8 hours for rare ones, never for MVP-only items; each brings a batch. A better offer brings more. 200 = twice as often, 50 = half.

settings.label: Customers come while the server is off
settings.description: At start, your @autotrade stalls and buying stores get the customers of the time the server was off (up to 48 hours). The Merchant Guild mails you what happened while you were away: after a start, when a stall closes, and every six hours.

settings.label: Dynamic market
settings.description: Prices follow the market: buying from the stalls drives a price up, selling to the buyers drives it down, and your own stall's trades nudge it. Related items move together, and every move drifts back to the price list over time. Fake stalls, buyers and your customers all use the moved price. The board at Prontera (131, 218) shows the movers.

settings.label: Market strength (%)
settings.description: How hard trades move prices. At 100, selling 30 Elunium to the buyers lowers its price about 5 %, 3 Angeling Cards about 12 %, 500 Jellopy hardly at all: the more of an item changes hands each day, the less one trade moves it. Prices stay between half and twice the price list.

settings.label: Price recovery (hours)
settings.description: How fast prices drift back to the price list: after this many hours, half of any move has faded (after twice as long, three quarters). Time the server is off counts too.

settings.label: Market news
settings.description: About once a week a news event moves a group of items for a few days: a War of Emperium season raising potions and gems, a guild flooding the market with Glast Heim loot, monsters migrating between dungeons. The board shows what is going on; each fades like any other move.
